The city, not the sphere; a 30 km disc around the site. keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1098-1522 (March 1522). The page's extent is undated and 'its expansion northward was halted by Aztec expansion into Oaxaca'; a disc of 89 km (about 25,000 km2) round the site stands for the sphere, plus Tilantongo in the Mixteca Alta. The Mixtec page: Eight Deer 'conquered and united most of the Mixteca region'. Soft in all respects.

ledger.note: 1083: Eight Deer Jaguar Claw founds Tututepec on the coast. 'migrates to the coast with a group of Mixtecs and founds Tututepec in 1083.' The Mixtec page has his armies 'conquered several major and minor kingdoms on their way to the coast'. Fix fx-49 (2 Nov 2026, request R041 of window p1000-p1099): the gazetteer has no 'Tututepec', so every Tututepec place in this dossier is now the disc {lon -97.600, lat 16.133} at the same radius; the point is the printed position of Villa de Tututepec de Melchor Ocampo ('16°08′N 97°36′W') on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_de_Tututepec_de_Melchor_Ocampo, the town which the Tututepec page says occupies the site (that page prints no coordinates).
1098: Eight Deer takes Tilantongo. 'In 1097 a Toltec delegation led by their leader Four Jaguar visited Tututepec' and aided him in conquering Tilantongo 'the next year'.
February 1522: the Spaniards reach Tututepec. 'in January 1522, arriving in Tututepec in February'.
4 March 1522: Tututepec falls. The Spaniards 'conquered it by March 4'.
4 March 1522: the Mixtec coast passes to Spain.
March 1522: the kingdom of Tututepec ends in the Spanish conquest.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of Tututepec
wars.outcome: The Spaniards, arriving in January 1522 and at Tututepec in February, conquered it by 4 March 1522.

wars.name: Aztec campaigns in Oaxaca
wars.outcome: Aztec forces triumphed over the Mixtecs in 1458 and built a fort on the hill of Huaxyacac in 1486; the Tututepec page records no direct interaction with the Aztecs and says its northward expansion was halted by Aztec expansion in Oaxaca.
wars.note: The Moctezuma II page has a conquest of 'Tototepec' about 1507 (in a passage on Atlixco, after Duran); whether Tototepec is Tututepec is not stated, and the Tututepec page contradicts a conquest.

certainty.note: The sphere of influence is approximate (an area of more than 25,000 km2); no border is known.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Mixtec states). Two pages (budget 2-5). (1) Extent: the page's 25,000 km2 is the largest extent and is undated; the keyframe from 1098 applies it to the whole later life (reading). (2) The Aztec relation is uncertain: the Tututepec page has no direct interaction; the Moctezuma II page records a conquest of Tototepec around 1507. (3) The Aztec dossier carries the Oaxaca events. (4) The Mixteca Alta kingdoms (Tilantongo, Coixtlahuaca, Yanhuitlan, Achiutla) and the Valley of Oaxaca Zapotec states are not given dossiers (counterparts_needing_dossiers); the Mixtec page gives only the 1521 Spanish submission (Orozco, 25 November 1521). (5) Gazetteer names needed: Tututepec, Tilantongo. Fix fx-49 (2 Nov 2026): the place 'Tututepec' (not in the gazetteer) is replaced everywhere by the disc {lon -97.600, lat 16.133} at the old radius, so the found event and both keyframes resolve and the state is drawn 1083-1522 (R041).
